review_status: reviewed 2026-11-14 - biology checked against NOAA Fisheries; Atlantic/Monroe recreational rules checked against current FWC guidance

profile.size: Large reef grouper; adults commonly reach several feet. NOAA describes fish occurring to about 200 m depth.
profile.diet: Juveniles feed mainly on crustaceans, especially shrimp. Adults primarily eat fishes and squid.
profile.swimming_depth: Near-bottom reef habitat from shallow water to about 200 m; adults move into progressively deeper water as they grow.
profile.behavior: Generally solitary and relatively site-attached outside spawning. Adults occupy rocky bottoms, drop-off walls, ledges, caves, crevices, coral reefs and artificial reefs. Juveniles use seagrass and oyster-rubble habitat in parts of the range; Florida Keys juveniles also use reef habitat.
profile.life_history: Protogynous hermaphrodite: fish begin life as females and some change to males as they grow. Adults aggregate to spawn; fertilized eggs are pelagic.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside ideal bounds for black grouper.
factors.value_notes: Reef Life Survey reports a broad observed sea-temperature range of 20.9–31.1 °C for the species. This is occurrence across surveyed reefs, not a physiological optimum or South Florida catch-response curve, and it does not validate the configured 20–29 °C range or 23–27 °C ideal as preferred SST.

factors.reason_template: Structure is {value}, where black grouper hold.
factors.value_notes: NOAA, Florida Museum, and FDACS describe adult black grouper using rocky bottoms, coral/natural reefs, drop-offs, ledges, and artificial reefs; juveniles use shallower seagrass/oyster habitat. This supports the broad reef/ledge/structure association, but does not validate the exact category score ordering or relative numeric map values.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in prime reef depth zone.
factors.value_notes: Florida Museum reports 6–33 m as a common habitat depth; NOAA and FDACS describe adults extending to about 200 m, with adults generally offshore and deeper than juveniles. This supports broad depth use but not the configured 10–110 m band or 20–60 m ideal as a locally calibrated preference. Depth remains an active gate.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.

regulations.summary: Atlantic/Monroe County: 24 in total length; 1 gag or black grouper per person per day combined, within the 3-fish grouper/tilefish aggregate; combined gag/black vessel limit 2. Open May 1-Dec. 31.
regulations.min_size: 24 inches total length (Atlantic, including all Monroe County waters)
regulations.bag_limit: Atlantic/Monroe: 1 gag or black grouper per person per day combined; 2 combined gag/black grouper per vessel per day; within 3-fish grouper/tilefish aggregate. For-hire captain and crew may not retain.
regulations.season: Atlantic/Monroe: May 1-December 31. Gulf rules differ; federal depth-area closures also apply.
regulations.jurisdiction: Florida Atlantic state and federal waters, including Monroe County; separate Gulf rules apply
regulations.source_name: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
regulations.notes: FWC states the Atlantic rules include all Monroe County waters. Gulf black grouper rules differ. Special regulations apply inside Biscayne National Park; consult the park-specific FWC rules before harvest. Reef-fish gear and landing requirements also apply.

open_items: The legacy SST range and ideal band are not supported by a species-specific thermal-preference study in the current record; treat them as provisional screening values, not a validated optimum.
Biscayne National Park species-specific size and bag restrictions need separate encoding before this record can provide park-level harvest advice.
